story: Shennong's mother swallowed the vapor of a dragon, and nine days later she gave birth to him on the banks of a river. He had the head of an ox with the body of a man. He grew rapidly, beginning to speak after only three days, and eventually reached a height of over eight feet. He obtained a mystical book of herbs from a Taoist master and journeyed across the land to record 365 medicinal herbs and fungi. He taught people the use of the plow, the basics of agriculture, and the use of cannabis. He was also called a god of burning wind, and was said to be either the progenitor of, or to have had as a minister, an ox-headed, sharp-horned, bronze-foreheaded, iron-skulled being. He was regarded as the father of a later ruler who carried on the secrets of medicine, immortality, and gold-making. Before his teachings, people were sickly, wanting, starved and diseased; he researched agriculture himself, eating hundreds of plants, and even consumed seventy poisons in a single day to test them, having a transparent body that let him see the effects within himself. He invented a bent-wood plow and cut-wood rake and established a noonday market. He discovered tea when leaves from a burning twig were carried by hot air into his cauldron of boiling water, and thereafter used it as an antidote to poisons. He eventually died after eating the yellow flower of a poisonous weed that ruptured his intestines before he could swallow his antidotal tea, having given his life for humanity. He was afterward worshipped as a healing deity and patron of farmers, rice traders, and medical practitioners. He is also said to have helped create a stringed musical instrument together with two other legendary figures.
